docs.title: Agent Continuity Layer Design
docs.text:
Date: 2026-05-05

Status: Draft design

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
DevCD should evolve from a developer-only context daemon into a local-first Agent Continuity Layer: a structured, policy-gated source of local context that helps any AI agent continue from the user's recent work instead of starting from a blank slate.

Developer workflows remain the first mature proof. The current system already records typed local events, updates state, retains scoped memory, applies policy, derives ambient context, exposes read-only MCP resources, and demonstrates Agent Resurrection through handoff packets. The strategic change is product framing and future architecture direction: Developer Context becomes the first Context Pack, not the full identity of DevCD.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
AI tools lose continuity whenever the chat window, model runtime, tool session, or agent role changes. Users repeat intent, constraints, prior attempts, decisions, artifacts, and blockers. Developer workflows show this problem most clearly because code, tests, Git state, and task notes are concrete and local, but the same continuity gap appears in research, writing, operations, learning, and creative work.

DevCD should solve the continuity problem without becoming the agent itself. It should keep observing local activity, shaping it into typed state, applying policy, and exposing safe context to local clients. The product promise becomes: agents can continue from policy-filtered local continuity, not from memoryless prompt reconstruction.

docs.title: Product Positioning
docs.text:
DevCD is a local-first Agent Continuity Layer.

It is:

  • a local source of typed continuity context;
  • a policy gate for observation, retention, and export;
  • a read-only-by-default bridge between local work state and agent runtimes;
  • a set of domain-specific Context Packs that translate activity into continuity concepts agents can use.

It is not:

  • a model;
  • a chat UI;
  • a task runner;
  • a telemetry service;
  • a remote exporter;
  • a workflow automation engine.

Developer Context remains the first supported Context Pack because developer activity is already modeled by DevCD and proves the continuity loop through Agent Resurrection, context briefs, and read-only MCP resources.

docs.title: Target Users
docs.text:
The Agent Continuity Layer should serve users who move between tools, models, and sessions while relying on local context:

  • developers who need coding, review, debugging, and subagent continuity;
  • AI power users who coordinate multiple assistants across local projects;
  • researchers who need continuity across sources, notes, hypotheses, and citations;
  • creators who need continuity across drafts, references, revisions, and style preferences;
  • founders and operators who need continuity across decisions, customer signals, planning artifacts, and execution loops;
  • students who need continuity across assignments, study plans, mistakes, and learning preferences;
  • knowledge workers who need continuity across documents, meetings, decisions, and follow-up loops.

These users should not need the same event sources or data model. They should share the same local-first continuity contract and policy boundary.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
The domain-neutral continuity model should be built around concepts that apply across Context Packs.

Concept Meaning Intent What the user or agent is trying to accomplish now. Activity A local observation that something happened. Artifact A file, note, document, dataset, task, branch, source, or other object relevant to continuity. Conversation A local exchange or session fragment that may carry intent, constraints, or decisions when policy allows it. Decision A choice made by the user, agent, or workflow that should shape future continuation. Attempt A concrete strategy or action that was tried. Blocker A failure, unknown, dependency, missing permission, stale assumption, or unresolved loop that prevents progress. Preference A user or project preference that should influence future assistance. Handoff / Continuity Packet A policy-filtered packet that lets another agent continue from local state. Withheld Context A safe explanation that context exists but policy denied raw exposure. Policy Decision The explicit allow/deny result and reason governing observation, storage, mutation, or export.

Developer-specific concepts such as file focus, Git branch, pytest failure, and code review map into these generic concepts through the Developer Context Pack. Other packs should provide their own mappings without weakening the shared policy model.

docs.title: Architecture Impact
docs.text:
The current architecture remains valid. The change is an architectural orientation for future work rather than a request to rewrite existing slices.

Existing responsibilities stay in place:

  • events owns normalized event contracts;
  • host_state_engine owns the local typed state tree;
  • memory_layer owns scoped local memory;
  • policy_layer owns allow/deny decisions and explanations;
  • ambient_context owns derived work-state, context surfaces, and handoff behavior;
  • mcp_server exposes read-only local resources.

Future Agent Continuity work should extend these boundaries carefully:

  • Generic continuity concepts should first live in the ambient context model where they are derived and exported.
  • Context Pack-specific normalization should live near the source or owning slice that understands the domain.
  • Shared kernel code should appear only after at least two packs need the same deterministic primitive.
  • Policy decisions must remain explicit for observation, retention, mutation, and export.
  • Remote export and write-capable agent actions remain out of scope unless a later ADR explicitly defines the policy boundary.

The architecture should avoid creating a second policy engine or a parallel domain model for every pack. Context Packs specialize event interpretation; they do not bypass the common continuity and policy layer.

docs.title: Context Pack Model
docs.text:
A Context Pack is a domain-owned mapping from local activity into continuity concepts. It defines which event sources matter, which artifacts and attempts are meaningful, which blockers can be recognized, which preferences may be retained, and which surfaces are safe to expose.

The first pack is Developer Context. It maps IDE events, Git state, task notes, test failures, code changes, review activity, and local recipes into active intent, relevant artifacts, attempts, blockers, next actions, and withheld context.

Future packs may include Research Context, Creator Context, Operator Context, Learning Context, or Knowledge Work Context. These are directions, not connector commitments. A new pack should not be added until there is a concrete local event source, a policy model, documentation, and tests that prove it can produce useful continuity without remote export.

A Context Pack should define:

  • domain scope and non-goals;
  • accepted local event classes;
  • artifact types and identifiers;
  • mappings into Intent, Activity, Artifact, Conversation, Decision, Attempt, Blocker, and Preference;
  • default policy expectations and sensitive payload classes;
  • surfaces it supports;
  • packet fields it contributes;
  • examples and fixtures that demonstrate continuity.

docs.title: Generic Surface Model
docs.text:
DevCD already treats context surfaces as product primitives for coding agents, review agents, debugging agents, subagents, and public demos. The Agent Continuity Layer should generalize this model without losing the role-aware behavior.

A surface should describe the intended consumer, allowed continuity concepts, allowed memory scopes, detail level, and withheld fields. Surfaces are applied after policy. A surface can reduce what an allowed export contains, but it cannot reveal context that policy denied.

The generic model should support surfaces such as:

  • coding-agent, review-agent, and debugging-agent for the Developer Context Pack;
  • subagent for narrow delegated work;
  • public-demo for safe examples;
  • future domain surfaces such as research-agent, writing-agent, or operator-agent only when their packs are implemented.

Transport names such as CLI, HTTP, MCP, and future local adapters should remain separate from product surfaces. Transport answers how context is delivered; surface answers what continuity shape is safe and useful for the consumer.

docs.title: Handoff Evolution
docs.text:
The current agent handoff packet proves the core capability: a new coding agent can see active goal, latest failure, last attempted fix, why it failed, do-not-repeat guidance, suggested next action, and withheld-context summaries.

The next abstraction should be Continuity Packet. A Continuity Packet is the domain-neutral form of the handoff packet. It should preserve compatibility with the current developer handoff packet while making room for non-developer packs.

A Continuity Packet should contain:

  • packet identity, schema version, generated time, pack, and surface;
  • active intent;
  • relevant artifacts;
  • recent activities and attempts;
  • decisions that affect continuation;
  • blockers and unresolved loops;
  • preferences that policy allows the agent to use;
  • suggested next actions when they are derived from visible local context;
  • withheld context entries with safe summaries and policy reasons;
  • the policy decision that authorized the export;
  • provenance linking packet sections back to local event classes or state areas, not raw sensitive payloads.

The current devcd://context/agent-handoff-packet MCP resource and devcd context handoff-demo --json command should be treated as the Developer Context Pack's current packet surface. A later implementation can add a domain-neutral name while preserving the existing contract until a migration path is documented.

docs.title: Phase 0: Product language and docs
docs.text:
• Document DevCD as a local-first Agent Continuity Layer.
  • Clarify that Developer Context is the first Context Pack.
  • Keep existing README and docs grounded in the current developer proof.
  • Avoid claiming support for non-developer connectors before local packs exist.

docs.title: Phase 1: Domain-neutral model draft
docs.text:
• Define typed continuity concepts in the ambient context domain.
  • Map existing Developer Context fields to domain-neutral names.
  • Keep existing handoff packet and schema compatible.
  • Add tests that prove the developer handoff still works.

docs.title: Phase 2: Context Pack registry shape
docs.text:
• Introduce a minimal local registry or configuration shape for Context Packs only when a second pack or a pack boundary test requires it.
  • Define pack metadata, event class ownership, supported surfaces, and packet contributions.
  • Keep pack behavior local and policy-gated.

docs.title: Phase 3: Continuity Packet contract
docs.text:
• Add a domain-neutral Continuity Packet schema alongside the existing agent handoff packet schema.
  • Provide compatibility rendering for the current Developer Context packet.
  • Expose the packet through existing local transports without adding write capabilities.

docs.title: Phase 4: Second pack proof
docs.text:
• Choose one narrow non-developer pack only after there is a concrete local event source and strong privacy story.
  • Build a small fixture-driven demo comparable to Agent Resurrection.
  • Validate that the shared continuity concepts hold outside developer work.

docs.title: Phase 5: Pack authoring guidance
docs.text:
• Document how to propose a Context Pack.
  • Require local event sources, policy defaults, fixtures, tests, and non-goals.
  • Keep remote sync, telemetry, and hosted agent behavior outside the default product boundary.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Product language may get broader than implemented capability. Mitigation: keep developer workflows as the current proof and label future packs as directions.
  • Generic concepts may become too abstract for agents to use. Mitigation: every concept must map to concrete packet fields and fixtures.
  • Context Packs may duplicate policy behavior. Mitigation: packs specialize interpretation, while policy_layer remains authoritative for allow/deny.
  • Surface and transport concepts may blur. Mitigation: document surfaces as consumer views and transports as delivery mechanisms.
  • Continuity Packet migration may break existing MCP or CLI consumers. Mitigation: add the neutral contract alongside the current handoff packet and preserve compatibility until a deprecation path exists.
  • Non-developer domains may invite sensitive data capture. Mitigation: require explicit policy defaults, withheld-context behavior, and local fixtures before adding packs.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• What is the smallest second Context Pack that proves the model without adding risky connectors?
  • Should Context Pack metadata be static code, local configuration, or both?
  • How should pack-specific preferences be corrected, expired, or deleted through the existing memory controls?
  • What packet fields must be stable across all packs, and which fields may be pack-specific extensions?
  • When should the MCP resource gain a domain-neutral Continuity Packet URI, and how long should the current agent handoff URI remain canonical?
  • How should future docs balance the broader Agent Continuity identity with the current Developer Context proof?

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• The strategic docs describe DevCD as a local-first Agent Continuity Layer.
  • Developer Context is explicitly the first Context Pack and current proof.
  • The core continuity concepts are named and mapped to future architecture.
  • Handoff Packet evolution to Continuity Packet is defined without breaking the current handoff contract.
  • Local-first, policy-gated, read-only-by-default behavior remains mandatory.
  • The document does not claim implemented support for future non-developer connectors or remote export.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
DevCD should actively prepare the next agent run without asking the user to perform context bookkeeping. The MVP will let DevCD start configured local agent CLI processes as Scout Runners, collect structured Scout Reports, validate those reports through policy, and synthesize an Action Packet that primes the next agent.

This is not a move toward a larger deterministic context parser. DevCD will keep the deterministic pieces small: task contracts, runner allowlists, policy gates, output bounds, evidence validation, and Action Packet schemas. The context judgment itself can be delegated to local agents.

docs.title: Product Hypothesis
docs.text:
The next useful step after agent runtimes such as OpenClaw or Hermes is a local agentic context-preparation layer. It does not compete by becoming a stronger assistant. It improves whichever agent the user already uses by preparing that agent before the first token: current goal, last failure, failed approaches, relevant artifacts, safety limits, and the next useful action.

The normal user-visible result is not a cockpit. It is that the next compatible agent starts prepared and asks fewer recap questions. Inspection surfaces exist for audit, correction, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: MVP User Flow
docs.text:
1. User initializes DevCD for a workspace.
  2. Local settings include zero or more explicitly allowed Scout Runner templates.
  3. A compatible command, API caller, or managed agent instruction asks DevCD for an Action Packet.
  4. If existing continuity is sufficient, DevCD returns an Action Packet without starting a runner.
  5. If context is insufficient and local runner starts are allowed, DevCD creates Scout Tasks and starts the configured runner.
  6. The runner returns Scout Reports as JSON.
  7. DevCD validates evidence, policy, output size, schema shape, and sensitivity.
  8. DevCD updates local metadata and returns an Action Packet.
  9. The next agent run uses the Action Packet instead of asking the user to recap.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Add a new vertical slice:

text packages/devcd-core/src/devcd/slices/agentic_context/ ├── __init__.py ├── models.py ├── service.py └── api.py

The slice consumes:

  • AmbientContextService for work state, continuity packets, context packs, and existing withheld-context behavior.
  • PolicyEngine for runner start and runner output decisions.
  • MemoryStore for policy-safe local summaries.
  • StateEngine and EventLedger only through established service boundaries.

The slice owns:

  • Scout Task generation.
  • Scout Runner command-template validation.
  • Local runner lifecycle status.
  • Scout Report validation.
  • Action Packet synthesis.

The slice does not own:

  • Event normalization.
  • General task execution.
  • Remote export.
  • Model provider management.
  • Write-capable MCP tools.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text: text ambient continuity -> ScoutTask list ScoutTask + RunnerCommandTemplate -> policy decision allowed local process -> ScoutReport JSON ScoutReport -> validation + policy-safe storage continuity + reports -> ActionPacket ActionPacket -> CLI/API/read-only MCP/agent-ready instructions

docs.title: ScoutTask
docs.text:
Describes a bounded context question for a local agent runner. Required fields: id, kind, prompt, surface, context_pack, expected_evidence, created_at, expires_at, policy_decision_id, and schema_version.

Supported MVP kinds:

  • identify_current_goal
  • inspect_latest_failure
  • find_relevant_artifacts
  • extract_do_not_repeat
  • propose_next_action

docs.title: RunnerCommandTemplate
docs.text: Describes an allowlisted local command. It must be loaded from settings, not from request payloads. It contains id, command, static args, optional cwd, and safe execution limits. Template expansion is limited to explicit placeholders such as {task_file}.

docs.title: ScoutRun
docs.text: Tracks one local runner execution. It stores id, runner_id, task_ids, status, timestamps, exit code, timeout state, output truncation state, and policy decision details. It never stores raw unbounded output.

docs.title: ScoutReport
docs.text: The structured result from a runner. It contains task_id, summary, confidence, evidence, recommended_action, withheld_context, and optional field-specific updates. A report without evidence is rejected or downgraded.

docs.title: ActionPacket
docs.text: The product output. It contains current_goal, recommended_agent_mode, next_action, relevant_artifacts, last_failure, do_not_repeat, unknowns, ready_for_agent, policy_summary, withheld_context, and evidence references.

docs.title: Policy Rules
docs.text:
Runner starts are denied by default. A runner start can be allowed only when all of these are true:

  • local agentic context runs are enabled in settings;
  • the requested runner id exists in the local allowlist;
  • the command template contains no free shell string;
  • the requested task kinds are supported;
  • timeout, concurrency, and output limits are inside configured bounds;
  • the operation is local and uses metadata-only context.

Runner output storage is also policy-gated. Raw stdout and stderr are never persisted. DevCD stores only bounded status, safe summaries, structured report fields, evidence references, and withheld-context summaries.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Add conservative settings to DevCDSettings:

text allow_agentic_context_runs = false agentic_context_default_timeout_seconds = 60 agentic_context_max_parallel_runs = 1 agentic_context_max_output_bytes = 10000 agentic_context_runners = []

The runner allowlist should support configuration through devcd.toml. The first implementation can model each runner as a Pydantic settings object with id, command, args, cwd, enabled, and timeout_seconds.

docs.title: API Surface
docs.text:
Local HTTP routes:

text GET /agentic-context/tasks POST /agentic-context/runs GET /agentic-context/runs POST /agentic-context/reports GET /agentic-context/action-packet

All routes use the existing app middleware: loopback plus bearer token.

docs.title: CLI Surface
docs.text:
Add a top-level Typer app:

text devcd agentic tasks devcd agentic run --runner <id> devcd agentic action-packet devcd agentic reports submit --input <path>

Commands support human-readable output and --json where useful. The default path should not ask the user to perform context bookkeeping.

docs.title: MCP Surface
docs.text:
MCP remains read-only in the MVP. A future or late-MVP resource may expose:

text devcd://agentic-context/action-packet devcd://agentic-context/scout-tasks

MCP must not start runners in the MVP.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Missing runner: deny with a policy explanation and return a safe status.
  • Runner timeout: mark run as timed_out, truncate output, store no raw output.
  • Invalid JSON: reject report and keep only a bounded safe failure summary.
  • Report without evidence: mark as low-confidence or reject depending on field.
  • Sensitive output: withhold content and retain only source/type metadata.
  • Concurrent run limit reached: deny or queue only if a future ADR explicitly accepts queueing. MVP should deny with a next-step message.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Use TDD for every behavior. Start with model and service tests before API/CLI. Process-launch tests should use a fake local runner or a controlled Python process that writes JSON to stdout. Tests must not require real external agent CLIs.

Required suites:

  • tests/test_agentic_context.py for models, service, runner adapter, and Action Packet synthesis.
  • tests/test_api.py for local HTTP contracts and auth behavior.
  • tests/test_cli.py for devcd agentic commands and managed agent-ready instruction updates.

Full validation remains make check.

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
Phase 1: ADR, design spec, and implementation plan.

Phase 2: Models and service without real process launch.

Phase 3: Settings and policy gates.

Phase 4: Fake-runner and subprocess-runner adapter.

Phase 5: API and CLI integration.

Phase 6: Agent-ready auto-priming and read-only MCP resource.

Phase 7: Docs, examples, and full verification.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• Which concrete runner templates should devcd init --agent-ready write first? The first code implementation should avoid hard-coding provider-specific commands unless they can be safely tested locally.
  • Should runner reports become ledger events immediately, or should the first MVP keep them in agentic_context memory only? The recommended first step is memory-only summaries, then ledger events once the report schema has settled.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Create an OpenClaw-facing continuity moment that feels native to how OpenClaw users work: a fresh agent starts by reading DevCD context, names the active goal, names the failed attempt, refuses to repeat stale work, and respects withheld context before asking the developer to recap.

This is not a demo-centered feature. The primary artifact is a small, reviewable OpenClaw Skill draft that can become a ClawHub submission after real OpenClaw end-to-end verification.

docs.title: Product Decision
docs.text:
The moment is: Turn-0 continuity before conversation.

A good OpenClaw agent using DevCD should begin with:

  • the active goal from devcd://context/action-packet;
  • the next concrete action;
  • visible blockers and failed attempts;
  • do_not_repeat warnings;
  • withheld-context summaries and policy reasons;
  • a one-line confirmation or correction prompt only after it has consumed that context.

The agent should not ask the developer to summarize the task when a ready Action Packet exists.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In scope:

  • Add a root skills/devcd-continuity/SKILL.md OpenClaw Skill draft.
  • Update OpenClaw integration docs to make devcd://context/action-packet the first-class resource.
  • Update the OpenClaw use-case draft away from legacy agent-handoff-packet wording.
  • Add tests that keep the Skill small, safe, and honest about claims.
  • Preserve DevCD's local-first and read-only MCP boundary.

Out of scope:

  • No OpenClaw plugin package.
  • No ClawHub publication claim.
  • No mutation of ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.
  • No automatic OpenClaw gateway management.
  • No live OpenClaw E2E verification claim unless a real OpenClaw runtime is executed later.
  • No new “demo” as the main product surface.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
This is a documentation and packaging-surface change, not a new DevCD runtime slice.

The Skill is a static artifact owned by the repository. It instructs OpenClaw agents to consume existing DevCD MCP resources. The runtime boundary remains the existing stdio MCP command:

json5 { mcp: { servers: { devcd: { command: "devcd", args: ["mcp", "serve"], }, }, }, }

No DevCD code should write OpenClaw config. Operators configure OpenClaw explicitly.

docs.title: Policy And Security
docs.text:
The Skill must instruct agents to:

  • prefer devcd://context/action-packet;
  • read devcd://context/policy-summary before asking about withheld context;
  • never request hidden payloads;
  • never treat DevCD as an action executor;
  • never start daemons, edit OpenClaw config, or publish packages unless the operator explicitly asks.

The MCP server remains resources-only and read-only. No new tools or prompts are added.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Automated verification should cover:

  • Skill frontmatter includes name and description.
  • Skill content names devcd://context/action-packet as the first resource.
  • Skill content forbids hidden payload requests and OpenClaw config mutation.
  • Skill content does not claim official plugin, ClawHub publication, or verified OpenClaw E2E status.
  • Existing make check remains green.
  • mkdocs build --strict --site-dir <temp> remains green.
